description: Native HTML autoFocus on a modal's first input silently breaks focus restore: it fires during React's synchronous DOM commit, BEFORE any useEffect runs, so it races ahead of the a11y hook's mount-time capture of the previously-focused element. description: `runLaneParamCallback` in src/actions/registry/runtimeHelpers.ts:787-821 returns `{ ok: true }` UNCONDITIONALLY for every lane action, because the dispatch is fire-and-forget (`window.dispatchEvent`) and ActionContext does not carry the live lane count. So although the human now sees a toast when a last-lane delete is refused, Teresa's own reply to the person chatting with her can still read as success. This is the program's signature anti-pattern - a layer reporting ok for work it never confirmed - one level up from the defect just fixed.
evidence: orchestrator-verified 2026-08-11 by reading the dispatch path; the same limitation is documented in the registry entry itself (processFlowActions.ts:732) rather than left implied-fixed.
status: PARTIALLY RESOLVED, updated by integrator 2026-08-12 (6fec03f7a0, commit b7868277de). `ActionResult` (src/actions/registry/types.ts) gained an additive `confirmed?: boolean`. 6 of 6 bus-dispatch sites (src/actions/registry/runtimeHelpers.ts, marked 'RISK-30 GRUPA A/B') plus the lane UI-closure branch now report truthfully via a correlated acknowledgement with a conditionally-armed 1500ms timeout, instead of the prior unconditional `{ok:true}`. The other 58 UI-closure sites across the registry degrade HONESTLY to `confirmed:false` rather than continuing to claim success. Sabotage (restoring the old unconditional `ok:true` on one lane action) -> rc=1, naming the specific action that should have failed; restore -> rc=0, 29/29. Registry counts unchanged (231 actions/124 runtime strings/7 events/4 API methods) - this was a semantics change, not a registry-shape change. RESIDUAL, stated plainly: `confirmed:false` still posts NO chat message on its own, so those 58 un-migrated actions can still read as an unchallenged success in Teresa's reply to the person chatting with her - only silence, not a correction. Mechanism this stream discovered that the original row did not know: `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx` (~L2043-2079) only posts an assistant chat message when `result.message` is set (`if (result?.message) { addChatMessage(...) }`), so a refusal that returns `ok:true` with no `message` string leaves the model's already-streamed 'done' reply unchallenged on screen - the gap is not merely 'no ack', it is 'no correction ever reaches the transcript'.

description: The Idea Table rendered EVERY row into real DOM with no cap anywhere, and CSV import was completely unbounded. STILL OPEN: (1) post-fix behaviour at N=5,000 and N=10,000 is NOT MEASURED - the cap bounds DOM cost by construction and the N=1,000 case was measured dropping from 1,000 to 500 rendered rows, which is a structural fact rather than a timing, but the OOM ceiling was not re-tested; (2) only CSV import has its own explicit guard - the other multi-row-add paths (AI add rows, framework apply, duplicate) are protected only by the render cap, so they can still inflate the underlying data set without telling the user; (3) virtualization remains the better long-term answer and is not done. All with localized user-visible toasts per outcome (ideas.table.aiAddRowsBlockedAtCap / aiAddRowsTruncatedAtCap / frameworkApplyBlockedAtCap / frameworkApplyTruncatedAtCap). TWO claims implicit in this row's original '(2) only CSV import has its own explicit guard' bullet are corrected here: duplicate adds EXACTLY ONE row (it was never a multi-row path in the first place - handleDuplicateRow is singular by construction), and 'bulk duplicate' does NOT exist anywhere in this codebase (grepped, zero hits). description: The shared CanvasContextMenu loses keyboard focus on close and never implements roving tabindex. After Escape, focus lands on document.body instead of returning to the element that opened the menu (node, edge or pane), and no [role=menuitem] ever carries tabIndex>=0. Affects all seven consumers: Mind Map pane/node/edge, Whiteboard edge, Process Flow, Idea canvas, Table.
evidence: orchestrator-bisected 2026-08-11 across nine commits: src/components/MyWork/canvas/__tests__/whiteboardContextMenu.keyboard.integration.test.tsx passes 4/4 at origin/demo (9d17cac114) and fails 4/4 from 93ebc3aa20 onward - this program's FIRST commit, 'E00: forward-port Ideas navigation/context-menu unification'.
status: RESOLVED 2026-08-11. Root cause: closeAndRestore scheduled focus restore in a requestAnimationFrame, but onClose() unmounts the menu synchronously inside the same React flush, so the rAF never ran before any assertion or, for a real user, before focus had already been lost to body. Replaced with an unmount-effect cleanup mirroring useDialogA11y's canonical restore. Roving tabindex added via an activeItemId state that follows the native focus event, so every existing focus-moving call site (open-focus, Arrow keys, Home/End) updates it without bespoke wiring. Named test 4/4 green and MATCHES origin/demo's 4/4 - orchestrator ran both sides; the test file was not modified. Orchestrator's own sabotage (removing the roving tabIndex) reproduces 'expected -1 to be greater than or equal to 0'. It also fixed 2 further tests in IdeaCanvasContextMenu.cb05 that were silently broken by the same cause and equally invisible under the old scope. Dead code noted: useAccessibleMenu.ts implements roving tabindex correctly and is imported by nothing.

description: Intl.PluralRules('jp') silently resolves to 'en-US' because 'jp' is not a valid BCP47 language subtag (Japan's real subtag is 'ja') - confirmed live: `new Intl.PluralRules('jp').resolvedOptions()` returns `{ locale: 'en-US', type: 'cardinal', ... }`. Any code path that uses Intl.PluralRules (or i18next's pluralization, which delegates to it) for the 'jp' locale therefore resolves plural categories by ENGLISH rules product-wide, not Japanese ones - a silent, pre-existing defect, wholly separate from RISK-26's translation-coverage gap.
